title: Java Exceptions
learningObjectives: Explain why exceptions interrupt normal control flow.
Use try and catch to handle expected failures.
Use finally for cleanup that must run.
Catch specific exceptions before broader exception types.

understand.concept: An exception is an object that represents an unusual condition during program execution. Java uses try and catch to handle failures at a suitable boundary. A finally block runs after try/catch completes in ordinary control flow and is commonly used for cleanup. Checked exceptions must be caught or declared; unchecked exceptions are RuntimeException subclasses. Catch the most specific exception that your code can meaningfully handle.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic equips Java learners to write robust programs using java exceptions in real applications.
understand.analogy: Think of each language feature as a clearly labelled tool: choose it for the specific problem it is designed to solve.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the Java language and library contracts; compile and test the actual behaviour.

explain.narrative: Place risky operations in a try block and add catch clauses for the exceptions you can recover from. A catch clause receives the exception object and may inspect its message. Multiple catch clauses are checked from top to bottom, so a subclass catch must appear before a superclass catch. Use try-with-resources for AutoCloseable resources; it is usually clearer and safer than manual close calls in finally.

examples.title: Catch arithmetic failure
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { try { int n = 10 / 0; System.out.println(n); } catch (ArithmeticException e) { System.out.println("Cannot divide by zero"); } } }
examples.explanation: ArithmeticException is caught so the program can continue.

examples.title: Catch invalid number text
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { try { int n = Integer.parseInt("abc"); System.out.println(n); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { System.out.println("Invalid number"); } } }
examples.explanation: NumberFormatException is an unchecked exception raised by invalid numeric text.

examples.title: Multiple catch branches
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { String value = "0"; try { int n = Integer.parseInt(value); System.out.println(12 / n); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { System.out.println("Bad input"); } catch (ArithmeticException e) { System.out.println("Zero divisor"); } } }
examples.explanation: Specific catch blocks handle different failure types.

examples.title: Finally executes
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { try { System.out.println("Work"); } finally { System.out.println("Cleanup"); } } }
examples.explanation: finally runs after the try block in this normal completion path.

examples.title: Catch a parent type
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { try { int[] a = {4}; System.out.println(a[3]); } catch (RuntimeException e) { System.out.println(e.getClass().getSimpleName()); } } }
examples.explanation: A superclass catch can handle a subclass exception, though narrower catches are preferable.

practise.guidedTask: Build a small Java program that demonstrates java exceptions. Predict the output before compiling with JDK 21.
practise.independentTask: Create a practical application using java exceptions. Include at least two test cases, expected output, and an explanation of one important edge case.
hints: Start with the smallest standard Java API or language construct that expresses the requirement.
Trace the execution path and verify the documented behaviour of each method or keyword.
Compile with JDK 21 and test normal as well as boundary or failure cases.
practise.challenge: Extend one example into a small reusable component and document its error handling, ordering or concurrency guarantees as relevant.

questions.prompt: Which block contains code that may throw an exception?
questions.explanation: The try block encloses code whose exceptions may be handled.

questions.prompt: Which exception is thrown by parsing non-numeric text as an integer?
questions.explanation: Integer parsing reports invalid numeric text with NumberFormatException.

questions.prompt: Where should a subclass exception catch appear relative to its superclass catch?
questions.explanation: Otherwise the superclass catch makes the subclass catch unreachable.

questions.prompt: Which block is commonly used for cleanup?
questions.explanation: finally is intended for cleanup that should run after try/catch.

questions.prompt: Which category must be caught or declared?
questions.explanation: The compiler enforces handling or declaration of checked exceptions.
